question: is the intact basement membrane shown in the figure, stained for elastin black?
reply: Yes. The thin, continuous black line tracing the inner curve of the wall is the elastic basement membrane (internal elastic lamina). In elastin stains (e.g., orcein or Verhoeff–van Gieson/iron hematoxylin), elastic fibers are rendered black, so an intact elastic lamina/basement membrane appears as that crisp black line — exactly as seen here. The pink band outside it is the muscular/fibrous wall and the yellowish region is the surrounding connective tissue/ground substance. So your answer of **yes** is correct.
